not_covered: The United States moved to force TikTok's sale or ban it primarily due to national security concerns regarding Chinese government access to US user data and the platform’s algorithm [Source: ev-1].
Legislatively, President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on April 24, 2024 [Source: ev-1].
The law required ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90 days) or face a ban in the United States [Source: ev-1].
On January 17, 2025, one day before the effective date of January 19, 2025, the Supreme Court upheld the law with a unanimous 9–0 per curiam decision [Source: ev-1].
The dispute was resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on June 10, 2025 [Source: ev-1].
The final resolution structured TikTok’s US operations as a joint venture rather than an outright sale, with ByteDance retaining a majority interest [Source: ev-1].
Under this arrangement, Oracle received about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, with SoftBank and other investors also participating [Source: ev-1].
Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations that facilitated this deal [Source: ev-1].
